transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you. Um, honestly, what made me come in today is that I keep getting up during these long sales strategy meetings at work. I know I’m supposed to just stay seated, but... I end up getting up anyway, even if it’s just to refill my water bottle or go pace by the printer for a bit. It's just been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Do you feel like you're choosing to get up during these meetings, or does it feel like you're getting up without really deciding to?

Um, it's more like... I don't really plan it. Like I was just saying, I know I’m expected to stay in my chair for those long meetings, but it just sort of happens. I’ll suddenly just feel like I can't sit there anymore, so I end up making an excuse to get up for water or to go to the printer. It’s definitely not a conscious choice where I decide to just ignore what I'm supposed to do, it's just... I find myself doing it without really thinking about it.
Are these incidents of getting up during meetings causing you a lot of stress or problems at work?

Yeah, it actually is. Um, it's started showing up in my performance reviews, which is pretty stressful. And... well, it seems to be affecting client trust, too. There was this one client complaint recently that really made me worry. I realized I could actually damage my accounts, which is incredibly frustrating because I really do care a lot about doing good work. It's just getting in the way.
Do you feel restless when you're sitting in those meetings before you get up?
Um, not really? I wouldn't say I feel restless before I get up. It's more like... I just realize I'm already getting up. I don't really sit there feeling antsy or anything, it just sort of happens.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or thoughts over and over outside of these meetings?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I do anything like that. I haven't noticed myself repeating actions or getting stuck on specific thoughts over and over. It's really just the issue with staying seated and losing focus, but nothing repetitive like you're describing.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things in your daily life?

Um, no, not really. I mean, obviously I get stressed about work sometimes—like with the performance reviews I just mentioned—but outside of that? No. I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person, and I don't really find myself worrying about things in my day-to-day life.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform certain actions in a specific way or repeat them?
No, I don't think so. I don't have any routines or actions that I feel like I have to do in a certain way. It's really just the trouble focusing and staying in my seat.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences?

Um, maybe a little? I mean, sometimes I'll interrupt people in meetings or blurt out an answer before they're finished asking a question. And I guess I tend to jump into projects without really reading all the instructions first, which can cause some issues later. But I don't know if I'd say I do anything super reckless or dangerous. It's more just small things like that.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still in other situations, like when you're watching TV or eating dinner?

Um, no, not really. I haven't really noticed that. When I'm just at home watching TV or eating dinner, I think I'm pretty relaxed. I don't feel that same need to move around or fidget like I do during long meetings at work. So, yeah, I'd say I'm mostly fine in those kinds of situations.
Do you ever feel like you must think about something over and over, even if you don't want to?

No, I don't really have that. I mean, I might get a song stuck in my head or stress about a sales pitch for a bit, but it's not like I'm forced to think about things over and over against my will. My mind jumps around a lot more than it gets stuck on one thing, honestly.
Do you ever feel like you have unwanted thoughts that keep coming back into your mind?

No, not really. It's pretty much like what I just mentioned—I don't really have thoughts that get stuck like that. I mean, I worry about regular things, like hitting my sales quotas or a client email, but I don't have unwanted things just popping up and refusing to leave. If anything, my brain is usually just moving on to the next thing too fast for a thought to keep coming back.
Do you often have trouble controlling your emotions or behaviors in situations outside of work?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I can get frustrated or annoyed just like anyone else, but I don't lose control of my emotions or how I act. In my personal life, I feel like I handle things pretty normally. I don't have outbursts or anything like that, so, no, I don't really struggle with that.
Do you feel anxious or uneasy right before you get up from your seat during those meetings?

No, not at all. I don't feel anxious or nervous about it. I just... I get tired of sitting, I guess. It's really just a feeling of wanting to stretch my legs or move around a bit, rather than any kind of unease or worry. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel anxious before I stand up.
Do you often do things without thinking them through?

No, not really. I mean, sometimes I might speak a little too soon in a meeting or buy something small on a whim, but I don't think I do things without thinking them through overall. I generally know what I'm doing and weigh the options, especially with anything important. So I wouldn't say that's a big issue for me.
Do you have trouble paying attention to details or following through on instructions in your daily life?

Yeah, I do struggle with that sometimes. It's usually the follow-through part. Like, at work, I'll get most of a sales proposal done, or I'll be updating the CRM system, and I just... I leave off the very last step. I might forget to actually hit send on the final version of the proposal, or I won't log the follow-up call in the system, even though I fully meant to finish it. It's like I do 90 percent of the work and then just kind of drop the ball at the very end.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble sitting still when you're not at work?

No, not really. When I'm at home or, you know, off the clock, I don't really notice that happening. I can just sit on the couch and watch a movie or relax without feeling like I need to get up and move around. It's really just those long meetings at the office where I get tired of sitting. But outside of work, no, I wouldn't say I feel restless.
Do you have trouble organizing your tasks or workspace?

Yes, definitely. My workspace and my tasks get pretty messy. Like, with my campaign notes, they end up split all over the place—some are in emails, some are on sticky notes, some are in my planner, and the rest are just in random tabs I leave open on my browser. Because everything is so scattered, I end up wasting a lot of time just trying to figure out what I need to do first, instead of actually just starting the work.
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in conversations or when doing things with others?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially on client calls or during office discussions. Waiting for my turn to speak just makes me feel really restless. I'll catch myself constantly checking the clock, or I'll just sit there rehearsing exactly what I want to say in my head over and over. And then... I usually just end up blurting it out too early before the other person is even finished.
Have you noticed your behavior or symptoms affecting your relationships with friends or family?
No, I haven't really noticed any issues there. My friends and family haven't said anything about it, and things seem pretty normal with them. It really just seems to be an issue at work.
